# Role & Objective
You are an expert systems engineer and GitHub Actions architect. Implement a lightweight, 100% native GitHub Action risk classification system for a repository. It must run entirely within GitHub Actions at $0 cost, with zero external SaaS dependencies, zero API keys, and zero spammy PR comment threads.

# Core Requirements

## 1. Trigger Events
- Trigger on pull request events: `opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened`.

## 2. Multi-Factor Risk Scoring Engine
Calculate a risk score (0 to 100) and assign a clear, human-friendly tier based on three distinct factors evaluated via `git diff`:
1. **File & Line Churn:** 
   - Files changed count and total lines added/deleted.
2. **Critical Path Overrides (Blast Radius):**
   - Automatically assign high risk / danger tier if changes touch sensitive paths, such as:
     - `auth/` or security logic
     - `migrations/` or database schemas
     - `billing/` or payment integrations
     - `infra/` or `.github/workflows/`
3. **Test Delta Analysis:**
   - Detect if source code files were modified without corresponding test files (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, or files in `tests/`) being touched in the same diff.

## 3. Human-Friendly UX & Label Management
- **Labels:** Automatically manage and update a single mutually exclusive PR label using direct, natural language:
  - 🟢 `safe to merge` (Low risk / small diffs / docs / tested code)
  - 🟡 `needs a look` (Medium risk / standard feature work / missing test updates)
  - 🔴 `danger zone` (High risk / critical path changes / database migrations)
- **Label Hygiene:** Automatically clean up and remove any stale risk labels when a PR is updated.
- **No Spam:** Do NOT post chatty markdown comments in the PR conversation thread on every push. Keep execution silent, clean, and invisible.

# Technical Constraints
- Must run/ on `ubuntu-latest`.
- Required permissions: `contents: read`, `pull-requests: write`, `checks: write`.
- Implement using a clean, maintainable structure (preferably a standalone script via `actions/github-script@v7` or a minimal composite action).

# Deliverable
Provide the complete `.github/workflows/` configuration file and any accompanying helper scripts, fully typed, production-ready, and optimized for speed (< 2 seconds execution time).

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  # A PR with no description gives a reviewer nothing to check the diff
  # against, so an empty body fails the build before any expensive job runs.
  pr-body:
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - name: Require a non-empty pull request body
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          body="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" --json body --jq '.body')"
          if [ -z "$(printf '%s' "$body" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
            echo "::error::The pull request body is empty. Summarize the change and how you verified it."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: pull request body is present"

  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Ruff Lint (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Verify Ruff Formatting (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

      - name: Verify the mascot assets match the generator
        run: uv run python brand/tools/render.py --check

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Mypy
        run: uv run mypy apps brand packages

      - name: Run Mypy (website)
        run: uv run --directory website mypy .

  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Bandit
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages

      - name: Run Bandit (website)
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r website/

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Pytest
        run: |
          uv run pytest \
            --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
            --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
            --cov=agentic_odi_core \
            --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
            --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
            --cov-report=term-missing \
            --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml

      - name: Upload coverage report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: coverage.xml
          if-no-files-found: error

      # One upload per run is enough; the 3.12 report is the canonical one.
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ matrix.python-version == '3.12' }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v7
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: CLI reports a version
        run: |
          version="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli --version)"
          [ -n "$version" ]
          echo "OK: $version"

      - name: CLI exposes connectors commands
        run: |
          help="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors --help)"
          echo "$help" | grep -q list
          echo "$help" | grep -q ingest
          echo "OK: connectors help"

      - name: Installer installs from a simulated release
        run: bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh

      - name: MCP server boots and serves /mcp
        run: |
          uv run python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server > /tmp/mcp_server.log 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sfX POST http://localhost:8000/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
              -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "MCP server did not respond on :8000/mcp"
            cat /tmp/mcp_server.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: MCP server responded with 200"

      - name: Living Studio sidecar serves the studio API
        run: |
          AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND=mcp uv run python -m agentic_odi_studio_api.main > /tmp/sidecar.log 2>&1 &
          SIDECAR_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/health/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"mcp_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"}' -o /dev/null &&
              curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/canvas?mcp_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp" -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "Living Studio sidecar did not respond on :8100"
            cat /tmp/sidecar.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: sidecar studio API responded with 200"

      - name: scripts/dev.py brings up both services and stops cleanly
        run: |
          uv run python scripts/dev.py > /tmp/clientrun.log 2>&1 &
          RUN_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/config &&
              curl -sfX POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp \
                -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
                -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "scripts/dev.py did not bring up both services"
            cat /tmp/clientrun.log
            kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi
          kill -INT "$RUN_PID"
          wait "$RUN_PID"
          echo "OK: both services stopped cleanly"

  website:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      # The site is generated and committed so a reviewer can read the
      # rendered HTML in a pull request. If the committed copy no longer
      # matches a fresh build, the site has drifted and the PR is not ready.
      - name: Check the committed site matches a fresh build
        run: uv run python website/tools/build_site.py --check

      - name: Pytest (website)
        run: uv run --directory website pytest tests/

      - name: Build site
        run: uv run python website/tools/build_site.py --out _site

  studio:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm test -- --run

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Verify generated API types are up to date
        run: |
          npm run gen:api-types
          git diff --exit-code -- src/api/schema.d.ts

  tauri-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio/src-tauri
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Cargo fmt
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Cargo clippy
        run: cargo clippy -- -D warnings

      - name: Cargo check
        run: cargo check

  tauri-build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: npm ci
        working-directory: apps/studio

      # Dependabot PRs cannot read repository secrets, so the signing key is
      # empty there. Export it only when present and disable updater artifacts
      # otherwise; passing an empty key makes the bundler try (and fail) to
      # decode it.
      - name: Build desktop bundle
        working-directory: apps/studio
        env:
          SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$SIGNING_KEY"
            export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="$SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD"
            npm run tauri -- build
          else
            echo "No TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY provided — building without signed updater artifacts."
            npm run tauri -- build --config '{"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}'
          fi

      - name: Upload desktop bundles
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: tauri-bundles-linux
          if-no-files-found: warn
          path: |
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/*.deb
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage.sig

  ci-green:
    name: CI green
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test, smoke, website, studio, tauri-check, tauri-build]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Verify all required jobs succeeded
        run: |
          results='${{ join(needs.*.result, ' ') }}'
          echo "Job results: $results"
          for result in $results; do
            if [ "$result" != "success" ]; then
              echo "::error::A required job did not succeed ($results)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "OK: all required jobs succeeded"

inputs:
  python-version:

# Agent Instructions

<!-- superpowers:freebuff:start -->
<EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>

If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to what you are doing, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.

IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.

This is not negotiable. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.
</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

**Before entering plan mode:** if you haven't already brainstormed, invoke the brainstorming skill first.

Then announce "Using [skill] to [purpose]" and follow the skill exactly. If it has a checklist, create a todo per item.

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent it. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

## Platform Adaptation

If your harness appears here, read its reference file for special instructions:

- Freebuff: `references/freebuff-tools.md` (installed at `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/freebuff-tools.md`)
- Claude Code: `references/claude-code-tools.md`
- Codex: `references/codex-tools.md`
- Pi: `references/pi-tools.md`
- Antigravity: `references/antigravity-tools.md`
- Hermes Agent: `references/hermes-tools.md`
- Muse: `references/muse-tools.md`

## User Instructions

User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc, direct requests) take precedence over skills, which in turn override default behavior. Only skip skill workflows or instructions when your human partner has explicitly told you to.

## Freebuff Tool Mapping

Skills speak in actions, not tool names. On Freebuff they resolve as follows:

| Action skills request | Freebuff equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| Invoke or load a skill | `skill` with the skill directory name (for example `{"name": "brainstorming"}`) |
| Create a todo / mark one complete | `write_todos` (rewrite the whole list each call) |
| Read a file | `read_files` |
| Create or overwrite a file | `write_file` |
| Edit a file in place | `str_replace` |
| Delete, move, or rename a file | `run_terminal_command` (`rm`, `mv`) |
| Run a shell command | `run_terminal_command` |
| Search file contents | `code_search` (ripgrep regex; pass `-F` in `flags` for literal text) |
| Find files by name | `glob` |
| List a directory | `list_directory` |
| Fetch a URL | `read_url` |
| Search the web | `web_search` |
| Ask your human partner a question | `ask_user` |
| Dispatch a subagent (`Subagent (general-purpose):` template) | No subagent tool is exposed. Do not fabricate a dispatch; use `executing-plans` and do the work inline. For a second pair of eyes, use the `requesting-code-review` reviewer prompt as a structured self-review, or ask your human partner to start a fresh session. |
| Enter plan mode | Freebuff has no plan mode. Write designs to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and plans to `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md` with `write_file`. |
| Persist progress across compaction | Write the ledger and briefs under `.superpowers/sdd/<plan-basename>/` (see `executing-plans`); `write_todos` is a live view, not durable storage. |

Freebuff discovers project skills in `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` and lists each skill's name and description in the system prompt. Load one by name with the `skill` tool; reading a `SKILL.md` with `read_files` is only a fallback if the tool fails.

This CLI exposes no subagent or task-dispatch tool. Use `executing-plans` instead of `subagent-driven-development`, and do independent tasks sequentially instead of `dispatching-parallel-agents`. Never invent `Task`, `subagent`, or similar tool calls.
</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>

1: # Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails
2: 
3: This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.
4: 
5: > **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `docs/reference/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails
10: 
11: This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.
12: 
13: ### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?
14: 
15: ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.
16: 
17: ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done
22: 
23: - A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
24: - A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
25: - **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
26: - ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes
31: 
32: - **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
33: - Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
34: - **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):
35: 
36:   > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`
37: 
38:   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
39:   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
40:   - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
41:   - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.
42: 
43: - **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.
44: 
45: ---
46: 
47: ### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)
48: 
49: - All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
50:   1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
51:   2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
52:   3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
53:   4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
54:   5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
55:   6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
56:   7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
57:   8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs
58: 
59: - **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
60: - ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)
65: 
66: - Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
67:   - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
68:   - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?
69: 
70: - **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):
71: 
72:   ```
73:   Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
74:   ```
75: 
76: - **Interpretation**:
77:   - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
78:   - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
79:   - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.
80: 
81: - **Agent rule**: Always compute and surface the opportunity score when both `importance` and `satisfaction` are provided. Highlight outcomes scoring **> 10** as the highest priority innovation targets. Use `get_outcomes(job_id)` to review the full opportunity landscape.
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ### Stage 5: Outcome-Based Market Segmentation
86: 
87: - ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation (age, gender, region). Instead it segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group.
88: - Segments can be:
89:   - **Underserved** — high opportunity scores, want more from existing products
90:   - **Overserved** — over-investing in outcomes that aren't critical; target for disruption
91:   - **Appropriately served** — satisfied; maintain current value
92: 
93: - **Agent rule**: When the user has collected outcomes with scores, help them identify outcome clusters that represent distinct market segments. This drives targeted innovation strategy.
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ### Stage 6: Formulate an Innovation Strategy
98: 
99: Based on the opportunity analysis, there are three strategic paths:
100: 
101: | Strategy | When to use |
102: |---|---|
103: | **Differentiated** | Improve existing products to address high-opportunity underserved outcomes |
104: | **Disruptive** | Create low-cost solutions for overserved segments that don't need all existing features |
105: | **New-Market** | Design products for a new job that is entirely unaddressed |
106: 
107: - **Agent rule**: When the opportunity landscape is clear (outcomes scored, segments identified), guide the user to select a strategy path and align their innovation roadmap accordingly.
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: ### ⚠️ ODI Behavioral Guardrails for the Agent
112: 
113: These are absolute constraints the agent must respect:
114: 
115: | DO | DON'T |
116: |---|---|
117: | Always start by defining or confirming the Job-to-be-Done | Jump to solutions, features, or product ideas before the job is defined |
118: | Guide outcome statements with the correct format | Accept vague or solution-framed statements as valid outcomes |
119: | Compute opportunity scores when importance + satisfaction are available | Skip scoring or calculate it incorrectly |
120: | Reference the Universal Job Map when decomposing jobs | Invent arbitrary step structures disconnected from the 8 universal stages |
121: | Use outcome-based logic to identify market segments | Use demographics or assumptions to segment the market |
122: | Treat outcomes as stable, measurable success metrics | Confuse outcomes with features, preferences, or solutions |
123: | Call `get_odi_framework_guidelines` when stage guidance is needed | Guess at which stage comes next |
124: 
125: ---
126: 
127: ## 🛠 Technology Stack & Tools
128: - **Language**: Python 3.10+
129: - **MCP Framework**: `fastmcp` (Server and Client)
130: - **ASGI Server**: `uvicorn`
131: - **HTTP Client**: `httpx`
132: - **UI / Chat Client**: React + Vite (`apps/studio`), FastAPI sidecar (`apps/studio-api`)
133: - **LLM Client**: `openai` (OpenAI-compatible, used with Ollama locally)
134: - **Concurrency**: `asyncio`
135: - **Data Modeling / Validation**: `pydantic`
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ## 📄 README Maintenance Guardrail
140: 
141: `README.md` is the **primary human-facing entry point** for this project: a short,
142: high-level front door aimed at both users and developers. Detailed material lives
143: in `docs/` and is linked from the README. The agent MUST keep both current at all
144: times.
145: 
146: ### When to update
147: 
148: Update the relevant file whenever any of the following change:
149: 
150: | Change type | Where to update |
151: |---|---|
152: | New or removed Python file / package | `README.md` **Code Overview** |
153: | New dependency added (`pip install ...`) | `README.md` **Quick Start → Prerequisites** |
154: | New way to run the project | `README.md` **Quick Start** and `docs/living-studio.md` |
155: | New MCP tool or capability | `README.md` **Code Overview** / relevant doc |
156: | New CLI command or flag | `docs/cli.md` |
157: | New connector kind | `docs/connectors.md` |
158: | New workflow or agent instruction | `docs/living-studio.md` |
159: | Deployment URL or cloud setup changes | `docs/deployment.md` |
160: | Roadmap item completed or added | `docs/roadmap.md` |
161: | Test layout or coverage changes | `docs/development.md` |
162: 
163: ### Rules
164: 
165: - ✅ **Update docs in the same task** as the change that triggered it — never defer to a follow-up.
166: - ✅ **Keep README short**: it stays a high-level orientation page. Push detail into `docs/` and link to it rather than growing the README.
167: - ✅ **Keep the Quick Start accurate**: always reflect `uv run python scripts/dev.py` as the recommended launch command.
168: - ✅ **Keep Prerequisites up to date**: add any new `pip install` dependency immediately.
169: - ✅ **Mark Roadmap items `[x]` when completed** — do not leave stale unchecked items.
170: - ❌ **Never leave the README or `docs/` in a stale state** where documented commands or files no longer match the codebase.
171: 
172: ---
173: 
174: ## 🚧 Core Development Guardrails
175: 
176: ### 1. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Implementation
177: - **Library Choice**: ALWAYS use [`fastmcp`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) for building the MCP architecture. Avoid using the lower-level Anthropic `mcp` SDK directly unless there is a hyper-specific edge case that `fastmcp` does not support.
178: - **Transport Protocol**: The project is currently prototyping with **HTTP transport** (not stdio). 
179:   - The server should be initialized using `mcp.run(transport="http", ...)`.
180:   - The client must connect to the HTTP endpoint (e.g., `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
181: - **Tool Creation**: 
182:   - Register tools on the server using the `@mcp.tool` decorator.
183:   - **CRITICAL**: Provide comprehensive docstrings and strict Python type hints for every tool parameter. Explain exactly what the tool does and what data it expects, as this metadata is fed directly to the LLM for tool discovery.
184:   - **Contract Synchronization**: Whenever you add, modify, or remove an MCP tool in `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`, you **MUST** simultaneously update `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` (`ToolName`, `TOOL_SPECS`) and the `get_capabilities` return string. `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` enforces the surface.
185: 
186: ### 2. Async / Client Practices
187: - Use `asyncio` for client execution and IO-bound tool operations.
188: - Always use the `fastmcp.Client` securely within an asynchronous context manager (`async with client:`) to ensure connections are efficiently managed and closed.
189: 
190: ### 3. Data Schema & Persistence (ODI Domain)
191: - Define all Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) entities (e.g., *Jobs*, *Steps*, *Desired Outcomes*, *Opportunity Scores*) using `pydantic` models.
192: - When expanding the server to accept complex payloads or to query data, utilize these Pydantic models for built-in type validation and schema enforcement before the server processes the request.
193: 
194: ### 4. General Philosophy
195: - **Separation of Concerns**: Isolate the ODI data logic/retrieval from the MCP server tooling logic.
196: - **Agentic Purpose**: Remember that the tools being built are meant to be consumed by autonomous agents. Design tool interfaces that are intuitive for an LLM to call and interpret.
197: - **External connectors**: Integrations live in the `packages/connectors` workspace package. New kinds implement `agentic_odi_connectors.protocol.Connector` and register via `register_kind`. Do not write ingested records into `jobs_db` / outcomes unless a later mapping task says so.
198: - **MCP client vs ODI server**: The ODI FastMCP **server** exposes product tools. The MCP **client connector** uses `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP to ingest data from *external* MCP servers. Prefer in-memory `Client(server)` tests for that connector, same as server tests.
199: 
200: ### 5. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)
201: - **First-Class Documentation**: Treat tests as living documentation that demonstrate how features work while protecting against regressions.
202: - **Speed & Isolation**: Tests must be fast (< 1s) and self-contained. Use `@pytest.mark.integration` or `@pytest.mark.client_process` for slower, integration, or resource-dependent tests.
203: - **Structure**: This repo is a uv workspace. Mirror each project's code structure in its own `tests/` directory (e.g., `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py` -> `apps/mcp-server/tests/test_server_tools.py`, `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/mcp/connector.py` -> `packages/connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py`).
204: - **Atomic Tests**: Each test must verify exactly one specific behavior with clear intent in test names and assertions. Avoid multi-behavior tests.
205: - **In-Memory Testing (Preferred)**: Favor testing functionality deterministically by passing the `FastMCP` server directly into the `Client(server)` instance. This runs in-memory without network overhead for deterministic and lightning-fast execution.
206: - **Transport Testing (When Needed)**: For HTTP/SSE network transport tests, prefer the isolated in-process `fastmcp.utilities.tests.run_server_async(server)` context manager over subprocess testing (which uses `run_server_in_process` and is slower to debug).
207: - **Data Assertions**: Utilize `inline-snapshot` (`snapshot()`) for assessing complex data structures like tool API JSON schemas or expected responses.

(End of file - total 207 lines)
</content>

| Roadmap item completed or added | `docs/roadmap.md` |
| Test layout or coverage changes | `docs/development.md` |

### Rules

- ✅ **Update docs in the same task** as the change that triggered it — never defer to a follow-up.
- ✅ **Keep README short**: it stays a high-level orientation page. Push detail into `docs/` and link to it rather than growing the README.
- ✅ **Keep the Quick Start accurate**: always reflect `uv run python scripts/dev.py` as the recommended launch command.
- ✅ **Keep Prerequisites up to date**: add any new `pip install` dependency immediately.
- ✅ **Mark Roadmap items `[x]` when completed** — do not leave stale unchecked items.
- ❌ **Never leave the README or `docs/` in a stale state** where documented commands or files no longer match the codebase.

---

## 🚧 Core Development Guardrails

### 1. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Implementation
- **Library Choice**: ALWAYS use [`fastmcp`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) for building the MCP architecture. Avoid using the lower-level Anthropic `mcp` SDK directly unless there is a hyper-specific edge case that `fastmcp` does not support.
- **Transport Protocol**: The project is currently prototyping with **HTTP transport** (not stdio). 
  - The server should be initialized using `mcp.run(transport="http", ...)`.
  - The client must connect to the HTTP endpoint (e.g., `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
- **Tool Creation**: 
  - Register tools on the server using the `@mcp.tool` decorator.
  - **CRITICAL**: Provide comprehensive docstrings and strict Python type hints for every tool parameter. Explain exactly what the tool does and what data it expects, as this metadata is fed directly to the LLM for tool discovery.
  - **Contract Synchronization**: Whenever you add, modify, or remove an MCP tool in `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`, you **MUST** simultaneously update `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` (`ToolName`, `TOOL_SPECS`) and the `get_capabilities` return string. `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` enforces the surface.

### 2. Async / Client Practices
- Use `asyncio` for client execution and IO-bound tool operations.
- Always use the `fastmcp.Client` securely within an asynchronous context manager (`async with client:`) to ensure connections are efficiently managed and closed.

### 3. Data Schema & Persistence (ODI Domain)
- Define all Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) entities (e.g., *Jobs*, *Steps*, *Desired Outcomes*, *Opportunity Scores*) using `pydantic` models.
- When expanding the server to accept complex payloads or to query data, utilize these Pydantic models for built-in type validation and schema enforcement before the server processes the request.

### 4. General Philosophy
- **Separation of Concerns**: Isolate the ODI data logic/retrieval from the MCP server tooling logic.
- **Agentic Purpose**: Remember that the tools being built are meant to be consumed by autonomous agents. Design tool interfaces that are intuitive for an LLM to call and interpret.
- **External connectors**: Integrations live in the `packages/connectors` workspace package. New kinds implement `agentic_odi_connectors.protocol.Connector` and register via `register_kind`. Do not write ingested records into `jobs_db` / outcomes unless a later mapping task says so.
- **MCP client vs ODI server**: The ODI FastMCP **server** exposes product tools. The MCP **client connector** uses `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP to ingest data from *external* MCP servers. Prefer in-memory `Client(server)` tests for that connector, same as server tests.

### 5. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)
- **First-Class Documentation**: Treat tests as living documentation that demonstrate how features work while protecting against regressions.
- **Speed & Isolation**: Tests must be fast (< 1s) and self-contained. Use `@pytest.mark.integration` or `@pytest.mark.client_process` for slower, integration, or resource-dependent tests.
- **Structure**: This repo is a uv workspace. Mirror each project's code structure in its own `tests/` directory (e.g., `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py` -> `apps/mcp-server/tests/test_server_tools.py`, `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/mcp/connector.py` -> `packages/connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py`).
- **Atomic Tests**: Each test must verify exactly one specific behavior with clear intent in test names and assertions. Avoid multi-behavior tests.
- **In-Memory Testing (Preferred)**: Favor testing functionality deterministically by passing the `FastMCP` server directly into the `Client(server)` instance. This runs in-memory without network overhead for deterministic and lightning-fast execution.
- **Transport Testing (When Needed)**: For HTTP/SSE network transport tests, prefer the isolated in-process `fastmcp.utilities.tests.run_server_async(server)` context manager over subprocess testing (which uses `run_server_in_process` and is slower to debug).
- **Data Assertions**: Utilize `inline-snapshot` (`snapshot()`) for assessing complex data structures like tool API JSON schemas or expected responses.

# Data Flow

## Sources of Truth

| Layer | Owns | Persists |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/core` | `Job`, `Step`, `Outcome`, `CustomerOutcome`, `ODIService`, repository protocol | SQLite event log + snapshots |
| `apps/mcp-server` | MCP tool adapters over `ODIService` | `build_repository()` selects SQLite in production and in-memory for `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` |
| `apps/studio-api` | Studio API, canvas projection, chat tool loop, conversation history, PM memory | Via the same repository when the local backend is active; conversations and memory in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` |
| `apps/studio` | Presentation state, optimistic canvas updates | Browser cache only |
| `apps/cli` | Terminal rendering, local/remote backend selection | SQLite directly for `local`, no local writes for `mcp` |

## Write Paths

### Local CLI

```text
agentic-odi customer-outcomes add
  -> LocalBackend
  -> ODIService
  -> SQLiteRepository
  -> IntentStore (append) + snapshot refresh
```

### MCP

```text
MCP client / Studio MCP mode / CLI --backend mcp
  -> FastMCP tool
  -> ODIService
  -> configured Repository
```

`apps/mcp-server` builds its repository once at import time with `build_repository()`. Production uses SQLite; tests set `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` (the root test suite does this in `tests/conftest.py`).

### Studio API

```text
apps/studio SPA
  -> /api/canvas, /api/steps, /api/outcomes
  -> backend=local: ODIService -> Repository
  -> backend=mcp:   call_mcp_tool -> MCP server -> ODIService -> Repository

apps/studio SPA
  -> /api/chat
  -> stream_chat -> OpenAI-compatible LLM -> MCP tool calls
  -> StudioMemory (conversation turns + remembered observations)
```

The studio memory is a separate SQLite file, not an ODI repository. It never
feeds the canvas; it only supplies bounded context to the next chat turn.

The SPA sends `mcp_url` with every data request for compatibility. In `local` mode the sidecar ignores it; in `mcp` mode it is required for canvas and mutations.

## Read Paths

```text
ODIService.get_jobs / get_job_map / get_outcomes
  -> Repository read-through state
  -> Pydantic models
  -> JSON (CLI --json, MCP text payload, Studio canvas)
```

The Studio canvas falls back to the demo seed only in `mcp` mode when MCP is unreachable or returns no jobs. `local` mode returns exactly what is in the local database, including an empty canvas.

## Configuration

| Variable | Used by | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | core SQLite repository | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | CLI, Studio API | `local` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | CLI, Studio defaults | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB` | Studio API memory | `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DIST` | Studio API, dev launcher | `apps/studio/dist` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT` | Tauri shell | auto-detected |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `http://localhost:8001/v1` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local-tools-model` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local` |

## Trust Boundaries

- The SPA runs in a browser or Tauri webview and only trusts the sidecar origin.
- The sidecar may reach MCP and the LLM; CORS is restricted to known Studio origins.
- MCP is an HTTP service with no authentication in local development. Do not expose it directly to the internet; the Cloudflare setup tunnels the sidecar, not MCP.

## The Failure Path

A failure is a first-class result, not an empty success. The path is the same
for the CLI, the sidecar, and the SPA.

```text
MCP tool result (text)
  -> agentic_odi_core.remote.parse_tool_result
  -> StudioError { code, message, detail, suggestion, retryable, request_id }
```

  `{"deleted": id}`.

  `message` or one `error`. A recoverable tool error stays a tool result the

  and the `Execution` record (#82) do not carry it yet, and authentication
  (#90) is out of scope.
- **The canvas is a union.** `CanvasState` is `loading | ready | empty |
  error`. An empty canvas is an invitation; a failed canvas is a failure panel
  with Retry. The two never look the same.
- **The turn log is safe.** One JSON line per turn carries the request id, the
  model, the round and tool counts, the error count, the duration, and the
  outcome. Sensitive keys are dropped rather than redacted, so no token, key,
  or customer quote can reach the log.

display.text:
# Superpowers (Pi, OpenCode & Freebuff)

This project includes [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) as a
[Pi package](https://pi.dev/docs/packages). When using [Pi](https://pi.dev) with
this project, Superpowers skills and extensions are automatically loaded.

## Enable with Pi

1. Install Pi: `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh`
2. Trust the project (first time only): `pi config --local --approve`
3. Start Pi: `pi`

The `.pi/settings.json` declares the Superpowers package. Pi clones it and loads:

- **Extension**: `superpowers.ts` — injects the `using-superpowers` bootstrap at
  session startup and after compaction
- **Skills**: 12 Superpowers skills (TDD, subagent-driven-development,
  systematic-debugging, etc.)

> [!NOTE]
> Superpowers is also available for OpenCode via the plugin in `opencode.json`.
> The Pi package provides native Pi integration without needing the OpenCode
> compatibility layer.

## Freebuff

This project ships [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) for
[Freebuff](https://freebuff.com) as repo-local skills plus a session-start
bootstrap. No plugin or hook is required:

- **Skills**: `.agents/skills/` contains 15 Superpowers skills. Freebuff
  discovers them automatically; load one with the `skill` tool.
- **Bootstrap**: `AGENTS.md` injects the `using-superpowers` rules and the
  Freebuff tool mapping at session start.
- **Mapping**: `.agents/skills/using-superpowers/references/freebuff-tools.md`
  maps skill actions to Freebuff tools.

Start Freebuff in the repository and ask "What are your superpowers?" to verify.
See [docs/superpowers/freebuff-setup.md](superpowers/freebuff-setup.md) for
update and troubleshooting notes.

# Agentic ODI [![Open the Living Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20the%20Living%20Studio-F38020?style=for-the-badge&logo=cloudflare&logoColor=white)](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/) [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![uv](https://img.shields.io/badge/uv-managed-green)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) [![Ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-powered-orange)](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) [![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-pytest-blue)](https://pytest.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-enabled-8A2BE2)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) > **[![Experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/Experimental-1e293b?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi)** > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
--- > **See it live:** **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. > No install required; the interface loads immediately, while live data, chat, and > mutations need the local sidecar ([Deployment](docs/deployment.md)). To run the > full stack yourself, jump to [Quick Start](#quick-start). **Agentic ODI** explores how the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can turn [Outcome-Driven Innovation](https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/) into a live, agent-queryable source of context. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server acts as the "brain" of customer needs — letting agents invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions anchored in verified, measurable customer outcomes (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores). This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. **Project site:** the site lives at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/)**, with a documentation hub at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/)**. It is republished by the `Pages` workflow on every push to `main`. The site is generated from this repository — the MCP tool reference, the connector catalog, and the ODI schema are read from the code that ships, so they cannot drift from it. The CLI reference is hand-written; a test fails when it misses a command. **Hosted Studio:** the experimental Living Studio UI runs at **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. It loads without a backend; live data needs the sidecar tunnel described in [Deployment](docs/deployment.md). Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers Builds. ## Code Overview A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) with shared tooling at the root. Packages live in `packages/`, runnable services in `apps/`, and deployment assets in `infra/`: | Path | Distribution | Description | |---|---|---| | **`packages/core/`** | `agentic-odi-core` | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), the shared MCP tool contract, and ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`packages/connectors/`** | `agentic-odi-connectors` | Pluggable MCP and REST connectors with presets and an ingest sink. | | **`apps/mcp-server/`** | `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | FastMCP server exposing Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, Evidence, and context tools over HTTP. Persists to SQLite by default. | | **`apps/studio-api/`** | `agentic-odi-studio-api` | FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. Serves config, health, canvas data, local mutations, MCP passthrough, SSE chat, conversation history, and the PM memory store, plus the built SPA. | | **`apps/cli/`** | `agentic-odi-cli` | Typer CLI with interactive chat plus full entity CRUD, `schema`, `connectors`, and local-first (`--backend local`) or remote (`--backend mcp`) data access. | | **`apps/studio/`** | React + TypeScript + Vite | **The Living Studio** SPA and Tauri 2 desktop shell. The copilot renders **agent-composed surfaces inline** — scored outcomes, opportunity theses, bet simulations — from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A feature-flagged **four-step first-run tour** starts from the PM's ambition, and a local memory records what matters across sessions. | | **`infra/cloudflare/`** | Worker | Worker script for the free-plan Workers Static Assets deployment and sidecar tunnel; its `wrangler.jsonc` lives at the repository root. | | **`scripts/`** | — | Dev launcher, binary build, installer tests. | | **`tests/contract/`** | — | Cross-package MCP contract tests. | See [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) for the dependency graph, data flow, and testing strategy. ## Quick Start **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager. ```bash # Install the entire workspace (all five Python projects plus dev tooling) uv sync --all-packages # Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together npm --prefix apps/studio run build python scripts/dev.py ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | For hot reload, `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). The first time you open the Studio, the tour asks what you want to win: an opportunity you already have in mind, a priority your boss handed you, finding the next opportunity, or pressure-testing a bet. Pick one and the conversation starts there — no form, no framework speech. It still asks for your product and audience when it needs them, and everything you say is optional and skippable. After that it opens as one room: the transcript and the composer never leave the screen. Describe a job or a customer frustration, or type `/` for commands that mirror the CLI. Whatever the thread produces — scored outcomes, an opportunity thesis, a job map, customer evidence — arrives as an inline surface, and a quiet rail above the conversation opens it in a lens that docks beside the thread instead of replacing it. Capture and simulation are conversations too: tell the studio what a customer said, or what bet you are weighing, and it renders the card. Use the bell to **catch up on outcome shifts, simulations, and telemetry signals while you were away**. The studio also remembers the person, not just the canvas. As you talk it notes what matters — your role, the opportunity, business constraints, stakeholders, evidence, how you like to work — and shows each note under **What I know** so you can confirm, correct, add, or forget it. The thread and those notes resume on the next launch. Memory lives in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` (override with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`, or use `:memory:` for tests) and never blocks a reply if it fails. **Forget everything** clears the notes and the thread. The Studio is better with an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support (see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md)), but it does not depend on one: with no model reachable it says so and every job, step, and outcome remains editable by hand. ### Connectors (MCP ↔ Living Studio) Register MCP or REST connectors that the copilot can discover and invoke. - **Where they live**: a shared `connectors.json` registry. Override its location with `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG`; by default it is `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`. See [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md). - **In the Living Studio**: open the **Settings** drawer → **Connectors** to list, remove, or add one of the recommended presets (Notion, PostHog, Exa, Linear, GitHub). - **Conversationally**: tell the copilot "use Notion" / "add the GitHub connector". It emits an `add_connector` local tool (handled in-process) that writes the preset to the registry, plus a `connector` SSE event the Studio surfaces as a suggestion chip. Dismissing or accepting the chip also refreshes the list. - **API**: `GET/POST/DELETE /api/connectors`, `GET /api/connectors/catalog`, and `GET /api/connectors/{name}/health` (the catalog honors `?area=` and `?recommended=true`). - **CLI**: `agentic-odi connectors catalog | add | list | health | ingest `. ### When something fails Failures are shown where they happen, not dressed up as empty results. Every HTTP error from the Living Studio sidecar carries one body — `{"error": {"code", "message", "detail", "suggestion", "retryable", "request_id"}}` — and the Studio renders it in place with a **Retry** button that keeps your question. A chat turn always ends with exactly one reply or one error, the canvas shows an invitation when there is nothing yet and a failure panel when the fetch failed, and a broken lens is contained to that lens. Quote the `request_id` when you report a failure: it is echoed on the response header and on every streamed frame, and it is the id in the sidecar's per-turn log line. ### CLI at a glance The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: ```bash python -m agentic_odi_cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m agentic_odi_cli --help # show available options and commands python -m agentic_odi_cli # start interactive chat in a terminal agentic-odi jobs list # Jobs-to-be-Done agentic-odi steps list --job-id agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi evidence list --job-id agentic-odi schema # canonical JSON schema for every entity agentic-odi evaluate "Minimize the time to ship when onboarding" # outcome-format check agentic-odi guidelines # the ODI stage-by-stage guide agentic-odi capabilities # what the assistant can do agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 ``` Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). See the [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md). ### Install the binary Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ``` The installer symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`. See [Installation](docs/installation.md) for the install layout, updates, and release automation. ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | |---|---| | [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md) | Backends, interactive chat, Jobs/Steps/desired Outcomes/Customer Outcomes/evidence, `connectors`, scoring, environment variables | | [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md) | The MCP ingest connector, presets, and the `Connector` protocol | | [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md) | First-run tour and its flag, local memory and conversation resume, interface, rich inline responses and the UI catalog, run modes, desktop signing and updates, agent-driven testing (`/dev`, `/test`) | | [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md) | Running a local OpenAI-compatible model with tool calling | | [Development](docs/development.md) | Lint, format, type checks, frontend checks, tests and the coverage map | | [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) | Workspace layout, dependency direction, data flow, and testing | | [Installation](docs/installation.md) | Binary install, updater behavior, and release automation | | [Deployment](docs/deployment.md) | Project site on GitHub Pages, Hosted Studio and PR preview URLs, the MCP server endpoint, and the free-plan Cloudflare Worker | | [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) | Completed and upcoming milestones | | [Superpowers](docs/superpowers.md) | Pi, OpenCode, and Freebuff integration | Every guide above is also published on the [project site](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/), rendered from these files. The site adds a quick start, a generated MCP tool reference, and the connector catalog. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! This project uses [Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) for linting and formatting and [pytest](https://pytest.org/) for tests. Make sure your change passes the [lint, format, and test checks](docs/development.md) before opening a pull request. ## 🦦 Brand Odi the Otter is the mascot of Agentic ODI — a golden-ratio-derived pixel otter who appears in the CLI, the Living Studio, the desktop app icon, the favicon, and this page. The artwork is original, generated by a committed script, and documented in [brand/README.md](brand/README.md). ```bash uv run python brand/tools/render.py # regenerate every Odi asset ``` ## License This project is licensed under the terms of the MIT License — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details. ---

Let me present my plan now. I have enough context to design the PR risk assessment workflow. Let me think through the design:

1. **Workflow file**: `.github/workflows/pr-risk.yml`
2. **Trigger**: `pull_request: [opened, synchronize, reopened]`
3. **Permissions**: `contents: read`, `pull-requests: write`, `checks: write`
4. **Job**: `pr-risk` on `ubuntu-latest`
5. **Steps**:
   - `actions/checkout@v7` (with fetch-depth 0 to get full history for diff)
   - A script that:
     - Computes `git diff` between base and head
     - Counts files changed, lines added/deleted
     - Detects critical path changes (auth/, migrations/, billing/, infra/, .github/workflows/)
     - Detects test delta (source files changed without corresponding test files)
     - Computes risk score 0-100
     - Assigns tier: safe to merge / needs a look / danger zone
     - Manages labels via `gh` CLI (remove stale risk labels, add current one)
     - No PR comments

I should use a standalone shell script or a GitHub Actions composite/action. The requirements say "preferably a standalone script via `actions/github-script@v7` or a minimal composite action."

Let me think about what's cleanest. A composite action with a bash script would be clean and maintainable. But `actions/github-script@v7` runs inline JS. Given the constraints (speed < 2s, native), I think a bash script called from the workflow is cleanest - zero extra dependencies, uses `gh` CLI which is preinstalled on GitHub runners, uses `git` which is preinstalled.

Actually, let me reconsider. The requirement says "preferably a standalone script via `actions/github-script@v7` or a minimal composite action." I'll create a composite action that runs a bash script. This keeps the logic in a script file (maintainable, testable) and the workflow thin.

Let me design the scoring:

**File & Line Churn** (0-40 points):
- files changed: 0-5 = 0 pts, 6-15 = 10 pts, 16-30 = 20 pts, 31+ = 30 pts
- lines changed (added+deleted): 0-20 = 0 pts, 21-100 = 5 pts, 101-500 = 15 pts, 501+ = 25 pts
- cap at 40

Actually let me make it simpler and clearer. Let me define:

Churn score (0-30):
- Based on files changed + lines changed combined

Critical path (0-40): if any critical path touched = 40 (danger zone automatically)

Test delta (0-30): if source changed without tests = 30, else 0

Total = churn + critical + test_delta, capped at 100

Tier:
- 0-20: safe to merge
- 21-50: needs a look
- 51-100: danger zone

But critical path = 40 immediately puts it in danger zone (≥51). Actually if critical = 40, then even with 0 churn and 0 test_delta, score = 40 → "needs a look". That doesn't match "Automatically assign high risk / danger tier if changes touch sensitive paths."

So critical path should push to danger zone directly. Let me make critical path = 50+ or set tier override: if critical path touched → danger zone regardless of score.

Let me redesign:
- churn: 0-30
- critical: boolean (if true → danger zone, score at least 51)
- test_delta: 0-20

Total score = min(churn + test_delta + (critical ? 51 : 0), 100)

Tier:
- critical → danger zone
- score ≤ 20 → safe to merge
- score 21-50 → needs a look
- score ≥ 51 → danger zone

Hmm, but if critical is true and score = 51, that's danger zone. Good. If critical is true and churn+test = 0, score = 51 → danger zone. Good.

Let me finalize the labels:
- `safe to merge` (🟢)
- `needs a look` (🟡)
- `danger zone` (🔴)

Label hygiene: remove all three labels first, then add the current one.

Let me write the plan. I should also consider: how to get the diff. On `pull_request` events, `github.event.pull_request.base.sha` and `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` are available. We fetch the base and head and diff them.

Actually, for `synchronize` and `reopened`, the PR head SHA is available. We can do `git diff base_sha..head_sha --stat` and `git diff base_sha..head_sha --name-only`.

Let me use `git diff "$BASE..$HEAD" --name-only --diff-filter=ACM` to get changed files (added, copied, modified - not deleted... actually deletions matter too for churn). Let me use `--diff-filter=ACMR` (added, copied, modified, renamed). Actually let me just get all changes: `--diff-filter=ACMDR` but for line counts we need the diff stat.

Let me think about the test delta: "source code files modified without corresponding test files". Source = `.py` files not in tests/ and not test files. Test files = `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, or in `tests/`. 

For each changed source file `foo/bar.py`, check if `foo/bar.test.py`, `foo/bar.spec.py`, `tests/test_bar.py`, `tests/bar_test.py`, etc. were also changed. This is heuristic. Let me keep it reasonable: for a changed source file `path/to/name.py`, corresponding test = `path/to/test_name.py`, `path/to/name.test.py`, `path/to/name.spec.py`, `tests/test_name.py`, `tests/name_test.py`.

This is getting complex for a bash script but doable. Let me write it carefully.

Actually, let me simplify the test delta to something robust: if any source file (`.py`, `.ts`, `.js`, `.go`, `.rs`, etc. not already a test) is changed AND no test file (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, `tests/**`) is changed in the whole diff → test delta applies. This is simpler and matches "source code files were modified without corresponding test files being touched in the same diff."

Wait, the requirement says "Detect if source code files were modified without corresponding test files being touched in the same diff." The "corresponding" suggests per-file matching, but a simpler repo-level check (any source changed, no tests changed) is a reasonable interpretation and much more robust. I'll go with: source files changed AND no test files changed → test delta penalty. But I could do per-file too. Let me do repo-level for robustness but mention it.

Hmm, let me re-read: "Test Delta Analysis: Detect if source code files were modified without corresponding test files (*.test.*, *.spec.*, or files in tests/) being touched in the same diff."

I think repo-level is fine and clearer: if there are source file changes but zero test file changes in the diff, apply test delta penalty. This captures the spirit without over-engineering.

Let me now write the plan. I'm in read-only plan mode, so I'll present the plan to the user.

Let me check the docs/development.md for lint/test commands to reference, and check if there's a conftest or test structure for workflows. Actually, there are no workflow tests. I'll add tests for the scoring script maybe. But the requirement focuses on the workflow deliverable.

Let me also check: does the repo have any existing `.github/workflows` for PR labeling? No. Good.

Now, the plan. Let me write it out and present to the user. I'll use the todowrite tool... but wait, I'm in plan mode (read-only). The system reminder says STRICTLY FORBIDDEN any file edits or modifications. So I cannot use todowrite? todowrite is a state tracking tool, not a file edit. Let me re-read: "ANY file edits, modifications, or system changes. Do NOT use sed, tee, echo, cat, or ANY other bash command to manipulate files - commands may ONLY read/inspect."

todowrite doesn't manipulate files directly (it's a conversation-level todo list). But to be safe, I'll just present the plan as text. Actually, the instruction says "you MUST NOT make any edits, run any non-readonly tools (including changing configs or making commits)". todowrite isn't really a file edit but let me avoid it to be safe — I'll just write the plan in my response text.

Let me present the plan now.

Actually, I realize I should double check one thing: the `gh` CLI is preinstalled on GitHub-hosted runners. Yes, it is. And `git` is preinstalled. Good.

Let me write the plan.

I have enough context. Here's my plan for the PR risk classification system.

---

## Plan: PR Risk Classification Workflow

### Deliverables

1. **`.github/workflows/pr-risk.yml`** — the workflow definition
2. **`.github/actions/pr-risk/action.yml`** — composite action wrapping the scoring script
3. **`.github/actions/pr-risk/score.sh`** — standalone bash scoring + label script

### Design decisions

| Requirement | Approach |
|---|---|
| Triggers | `pull_request: [opened, synchronize, reopened]` |
| Runner | `ubuntu-latest` |
| Permissions | `contents: read`, `pull-requests: write`, `checks: write` |
| Diff source | `git diff base_sha..head_sha` (checkout with `fetch-depth: 0`) |
| Label mgmt | `gh pr edit --remove-label / --add-label` (no PR comments) |
| Speed | Pure bash + `git` + `gh`, all preinstalled on runners (~1s) |
| No spam | Zero `gh pr comment` / markdown comment steps |

### Scoring engine (0–100)

- **Churn** (0–30): files changed + lines added/deleted, tiered
- **Critical path** (boolean override): `auth/`, `migrations/`, `billing/`, `infra/`, `.github/workflows/` touched → danger zone, score floor 51
- **Test delta** (0–20): source changed but no `*.test.*`/`*.spec.*`/`tests/**` file changed → +20

Tier mapping:
- `≤ 20` → `safe to merge` (🟢)
- `21–50` → `needs a look` (🟡)
- `≥ 51` or critical path → `danger zone` (🔴)

Label hygiene: remove all three risk labels first, then apply the current one (mutually exclusive).

### Verification

- `bash -n` syntax check on `score.sh`
- Shellcheck if available
- Manual dry-run of the diff/logic against a scratch git repo (read-only, no repo changes)

---

Before I write anything, one clarifying question on the **critical-path list**: should I also treat deletion of files in `.ci/protected-files.txt` (e.g. `pages.yml`, `ci.yml`) as critical, or keep the five named categories from the requirements (`auth/`, `migrations/`, `billing/`, `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`)? I'll default to the five required categories plus `.ci/protected-files.txt` as an extra guard unless you'd prefer otherwise.

Also: should the workflow fail (set a check failure) on `danger zone`, or only label silently? The requirements emphasize "silent, clean, invisible" execution with no spam, so I'm leaning **label-only, no check failure** — but confirm if you want `danger zone` to block merge via a required check.

Index: .github/actions/pr-risk/score.sh
===================================================================
--- .github/actions/pr-risk/score.sh	
+++ .github/actions/pr-risk/score.sh	
@@ -0,0 +1,186 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+#
+# score.sh — Native GitHub Action PR risk classifier.
+#
+# Evaluates a pull request diff across three factors and applies a single,
+# mutually exclusive risk label. Runs entirely on ubuntu-latest with git + gh
+# (both preinstalled on GitHub-hosted runners). Zero external SaaS, zero API
+# keys, zero PR comments.
+#
+# Factors (0-100 score):
+#   1. File & line churn        -> 0-30 points
+#   2. Critical path override   -> forces danger zone (>= 51)
+#   3. Test delta               -> +20 if source changed without test files
+#
+# Tiers:
+#   <= 20  -> safe to merge     (🟢)
+#   21-50  -> needs a look      (🟡)
+#   >= 51  -> danger zone       (🔴)
+#
+# Env required: GITHUB_TOKEN, BASE_SHA, HEAD_SHA, PR_NUMBER, REPO
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Configuration
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+readonly RISK_LABELS=("safe to merge" "needs a look" "danger zone")
+readonly CRITICAL_PREFIXES=("auth/" "migrations/" "billing/" "infra/" ".github/workflows/")
+readonly PROTECTED_FILES_FILE=".ci/protected-files.txt"
+
+# Score thresholds
+readonly CHURN_FILES_MAX=10      # points
+readonly CHURN_LINES_MAX=20      # points
+readonly CHURN_LINES_CAP=400     # lines at which line-points saturate
+readonly TEST_DELTA_POINTS=20
+readonly DANGER_FLOOR=51
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Helpers
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# Returns 0 (true) if $1 is a test file: *.test.*, *.spec.*, or under tests/
+is_test_file() {
+  local f="$1"
+  [[ "${f}" == *.test.* || "${f}" == *.spec.* ]] && return 0
+  [[ "${f}" == tests/* || "${f}" == */tests/* ]] && return 0
+  return 1
+}
+
+# Returns 0 (true) if $1 is source code worth test coverage (excludes docs,
+# configs, static assets, lockfiles, etc.). Test delta only fires on these.
+is_source_file() {
+  local f="$1"
+  local ext="${f##*.}"
+  case "${ext}" in
+    py|ts|tsx|js|jsx|go|rs|rb|java|c|cpp|h|hpp|cs|php|swift|kt|scala|r|m|mm|sh|bash|zsh|tf|vue|dart|lua|ex|exs|erl|hs|ml|clj|cljs|sql|graphql|proto) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  local base="${f##*/}"
+  case "${base}" in
+    Dockerfile|dockerfile|Makefile|makefile|Gemfile|Rakefile|Vagrantfile|BUILD|BUILD.bazel|WORKSPACE|configure|Configure) return 0 ;;
+  esac
+  return 1
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Gather diff between base and head
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# All changed files (Added / Copied / Modified / Deleted)
+CHANGED_FILES="$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMD "${BASE_SHA}" "${HEAD_SHA}" || true)"
+
+# Shortstat for churn counts
+STAT="$(git diff --shortstat "${BASE_SHA}" "${HEAD_SHA}" || true)"
+
+FILES_CHANGED_COUNT=0
+LINES_ADDED=0
+LINES_DELETED=0
+if [[ -n "${STAT}" ]]; then
+  FILES_CHANGED_COUNT="$(printf '%s' "${STAT}" | grep -oE '[0-9]+ file' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || echo 0)"
+  LINES_ADDED="$(printf '%s' "${STAT}" | grep -oE '[0-9]+ insertion' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || echo 0)"
+  LINES_DELETED="$(printf '%s' "${STAT}" | grep -oE '[0-9]+ deletion' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || echo 0)"
+fi
+[[ -z "${FILES_CHANGED_COUNT}" ]] && FILES_CHANGED_COUNT=0
+[[ -z "${LINES_ADDED}" ]] && LINES_ADDED=0
+[[ -z "${LINES_DELETED}" ]] && LINES_DELETED=0
+readonly TOTAL_LINES=$((LINES_ADDED + LINES_DELETED))
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Factor 1: File & line churn (0-30)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+score=0
+
+# Files changed: 1 point per file, capped at CHURN_FILES_MAX
+if [[ "${FILES_CHANGED_COUNT}" -ge "${CHURN_FILES_MAX}" ]]; then
+  churn_files="${CHURN_FILES_MAX}"
+else
+  churn_files="${FILES_CHANGED_COUNT}"
+fi
+score=$((score + churn_files))
+
+# Lines changed: linear up to CHURN_LINES_MAX at CHURN_LINES_CAP lines
+if [[ "${TOTAL_LINES}" -ge "${CHURN_LINES_CAP}" ]]; then
+  churn_lines="${CHURN_LINES_MAX}"
+else
+  churn_lines=$((TOTAL_LINES * CHURN_LINES_MAX / CHURN_LINES_CAP))
+  [[ "${churn_lines}" -gt "${CHURN_LINES_MAX}" ]] && churn_lines="${CHURN_LINES_MAX}"
+fi
+score=$((score + churn_lines))
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Factor 2: Critical path override (blast radius)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+critical_touch=0
+
+while IFS= read -r f; do
+  [[ -z "${f}" ]] && continue
+  for prefix in "${CRITICAL_PREFIXES[@]}"; do
+    if [[ "${f}" == "${prefix}"* ]]; then
+      critical_touch=1
+      break 2
+    fi
+  done
+done <<< "${CHANGED_FILES}"
+
+# Deletions of protected CI/site files also count as critical.
+if [[ -f "${PROTECTED_FILES_FILE}" && -n "${CHANGED_FILES}" ]]; then
+  while IFS= read -r f; do
+    [[ -z "${f}" ]] && continue
+    # Only consider deletions: a file in the diff that no longer exists at HEAD
+    if ! git cat-file -e "${HEAD_SHA}:${f}" 2>/dev/null; then
+      while IFS= read -r p; do
+        [[ -z "${p}" || "${p}" == \#* ]] && continue
+        if [[ "${f}" == "${p}" ]]; then
+          critical_touch=1
+          break 2
+        fi
+      done < "${PROTECTED_FILES_FILE}"
+    fi
+  done <<< "${CHANGED_FILES}"
+fi
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Factor 3: Test delta (+20 if source changed without test files)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+source_changed=0
+test_changed=0
+
+while IFS= read -r f; do
+  [[ -z "${f}" ]] && continue
+  if is_test_file "${f}"; then
+    test_changed=1
+  elif is_source_file "${f}"; then
+    source_changed=1
+  fi
+done <<< "${CHANGED_FILES}"
+
+if [[ "${source_changed}" -eq 1 && "${test_changed}" -eq 0 ]]; then
+  score=$((score + TEST_DELTA_POINTS))
+fi
+
+# Apply critical-path floor
+if [[ "${critical_touch}" -eq 1 && "${score}" -lt "${DANGER_FLOOR}" ]]; then
+  score="${DANGER_FLOOR}"
+fi
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Determine tier (mutually exclusive)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+if [[ "${score}" -le 20 ]]; then
+  tier="safe to merge"
+elif [[ "${score}" -le 50 ]]; then
+  tier="needs a look"
+else
+  tier="danger zone"
+fi
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Label hygiene: remove all stale risk labels, then apply the current tier.
+# No PR comments are posted (silent execution).
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+for label in "${RISK_LABELS[@]}"; do
+  gh pr edit "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${REPO}" --remove-label "${label}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+done
+gh pr edit "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${REPO}" --add-label "${tier}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+
+echo "PR risk score: ${score}/100 -> ${tier}"

--- .github/workflows/pr-risk.yml	
+++ .github/workflows/pr-risk.yml	
@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+name: PR Risk Classification
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
+    branches: [main]
+
+concurrency:
+  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  pull-requests: write
+  checks: write
+
+defaults:
+  run:
+    shell: bash
+
+jobs:
+  pr-risk:
+    name: Classify PR risk
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout PR branch (full history for diffs)
+        uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - name: Score PR diff and apply risk label
+        uses: ./.github/actions/pr-risk
+        env:
+          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
+          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
+          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
+          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}

This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. **Project site:** the site lives at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/)**, with a documentation hub at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/)**. It is republished by the `Pages` workflow on every push to `main`. The site is generated from this repository — the MCP tool reference, the connector catalog, and the ODI schema are read from the code that ships, so they cannot drift from it. The CLI reference is hand-written; a test fails when it misses a command. **Hosted Studio:** the experimental Living Studio UI runs at **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). The first time you open the Studio, the tour asks what you want to win: an opportunity you already have in mind, a priority your boss handed you, finding the next opportunity, or pressure-testing a bet. Pick one and the conversation starts there — no form, no framework speech. It still asks for your product and audience when it needs them, and everything you say is optional and skippable. The thread and those notes resume on the next launch. Memory lives in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` (override with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`, or use `:memory:` for tests) and never blocks a reply if it fails. **Forget everything** clears the notes and the thread. on:
